one_liner: Cloud CRM platform for sales, service, and marketing, with extensive REST/SOAP/GraphQL APIs.
access_detail: From background knowledge, not verified this session: free Developer Edition orgs at developer.salesforce.com/signup include API access. Customer production orgs need an API-enabled edition (Enterprise and above, or Professional with an add-on). Hosted MCP servers reportedly require Enterprise Edition and above. All developer.salesforce.com pages returned 403 to my fetch tool, so none of this was confirmed on the vendor pages.
blocker_detail: No blocker is expected: OAuth2 through a Connected App or External Client App can be set up in a free Developer Edition org. Salesforce has no classic webhooks; it uses Platform Events, Change Data Capture, and Outbound Messages, so a toolkit would need a different approach for triggers. Customers' orgs must have API access enabled, and some orgs restrict connected apps by admin policy. Not confirmed on vendor pages.

one_liner: CRM platform for marketing, sales, service with broad CRM/CMS REST APIs.
access_detail: Free developer accounts and free developer test accounts let anyone create an OAuth app and get credentials with no approval. Core CRM APIs work on free CRM accounts (not verified on the pages opened). Some endpoints need paid tiers. Marketplace listing needs review, but is not required to build.
blocker_detail: No blocker for building and testing. Marketplace listing needs app review, and some endpoints depend on the customer's HubSpot tier.

one_liner: Sales-focused CRM for managing deals, contacts, pipelines, activities and leads.
access_detail: Free developer sandbox account via developers.pipedrive.com lets you register OAuth apps and test without paying. Per-account API tokens also work. Public Marketplace listing may need vendor review; docs didn't detail this. Pricing page not opened, so a trial-only sandbox can't be fully ruled out.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker found. Public Marketplace listing of an OAuth app may need Pipedrive review (not confirmed in docs), but building and testing works with a free sandbox. Sanctioned-country restriction applies to developers.

one_liner: Customizable CRM platform for managing contacts, companies, deals and workflows.
access_detail: Free plan exists (3 seats, 50k records). Pricing page comparison table lists API and webhook access on all plans including Free. OAuth apps are created via the Developer console. The free-plan/API inclusion was read from a summarized page, so not fully verified.
blocker_detail: No blocker found. OAuth 2.0 for multi-workspace apps is documented; a free workspace should be enough for testing. I did not confirm whether public OAuth apps need Attio review before production.

one_liner: Open-source CRM with cloud and self-hosted options, REST/GraphQL APIs and webhooks.
access_detail: Twenty is open source and can be self-hosted at no cost, so a developer gets working API keys and OAuth clients with no approval. Twenty Cloud offers a 30-day no-card trial, then Pro at $9/user/month. I did not find a permanent free cloud tier. I did not verify the self-host license or Cloud plan gating of the API. The pricing page lists REST, GraphQL and webhooks on the paid tiers.
blocker_detail: No blocker for building, since a free self-hosted instance works. For testing against Twenty Cloud, the trial is 30 days and then paid. I found only community MCP servers and did not check whether Twenty ships its own.

one_liner: Work-management/lightweight CRM platform with customizable apps, workspaces, items, tasks and workflows.
access_detail: Register an app at developers.podio.com to get Client ID/Secret; a Podio account is required. A Free plan exists (up to 5 users, 100 items). Docs list no plan restriction on API access, but this was not explicitly confirmed. Rate limits are stated only vaguely, and the raise-on-request wording suggests approval is not required.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker found. Minor caveats: the free plan's 100-item cap, the 8-hour access token with a 28-day refresh token, and the official MCP is beta only. The pricing page could not be opened directly, so the free-plan and API-access details come from search-result snippets.

one_liner: Cloud CRM for leads, contacts, deals, and sales automation, with a REST API.
access_detail: Anyone can register an OAuth client for free at api-console.zoho.com, and the docs show no edition requirement for registration. The pricing page lists a Free edition (up to 3 users) with 5000 API calls/day, and paid editions have free trials. I did not confirm exact API-credit limits per edition, or whether the Free edition is still offered in every region and data centre. Each data centre (.com, .eu, .in and so on) needs its own accounts and endpoints.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker. Watch multi-data-centre endpoint handling and per-edition API credit limits. Zoho's paid-only sandbox feature was not checked, but the Free edition is enough to build and test.

one_liner: Sales CRM with built-in calling, email, SMS, workflows and pipeline management for sales teams.
access_detail: API access is on all plans (Solo to Scale), but Close has no free tier. A no-card 14-day trial gives credentials for testing, after which a paid plan is needed. I could not open the OAuth app registration page (404), so I don't know whether OAuth apps need vendor approval. Close's docs say OAuth is for third-party apps.
blocker_detail: There is no permanent free tier. Testing is possible only on the 14-day no-card trial, and continued use needs a paid plan. OAuth app registration and approval details were not verified.

one_liner: Google Workspace-native CRM for managing contacts, leads, opportunities, tasks and sales pipelines.
access_detail: API keys are generated by an Admin in Settings > Integrations > API Keys. The API is listed under the Professional tier and above, and a search summary said it is also available on trial. I found no free tier, and I could not confirm the trial length from the pages I opened. The OAuth2 app registration process for third parties was not verified and may need a partner or approval step.
blocker_detail: There is no free tier. API access needs a Professional or Business plan, or a time-limited trial. OAuth2 for multi-tenant use may also require a partner registration, which I did not verify.

one_liner: Intapp's CRM and deal-management platform for private equity, investment banking and financial services firms.
access_detail: DealCloud is an enterprise product with no public signup, free tier or sandbox found. The docs say an admin or the Customer Success Manager must enable API for a user group before users can generate a key. I did not find pricing or a trial page, so that part is inferred, not confirmed.
blocker_detail: Credentials come from a paying customer tenant. Each tenant admin must enable API for a user group, and the user then generates a per-user API key. This is the OAuth2 client-credentials flow with the API key as the secret, and the token lasts 15 minutes. There is no third-party OAuth app flow, and no free dev tenant was found. The official MCP server is read-only and in client preview since July 2026. The "webhooks" value comes from the Publications API, which the docs describe as events via topics and polling. That is not confirmed as push webhooks.

one_liner: Customer service suite: ticketing, help center, messaging, voice, and AI agents.
access_detail: No free plan. A 14-day free trial gives all Customer Service Suite Professional features, and the API works within it. After the trial a paid plan is needed (Support Team from $19/agent/mo). The pricing page doesn't say which tiers include the API. Global OAuth clients for multi-customer apps are created in the admin center. I did not verify sandbox availability, which is likely limited to higher plans.
blocker_detail: No free tier. Testing is limited to a 14-day trial, after which a paid Zendesk plan is required. Per-tenant subdomains are needed for OAuth URLs.

one_liner: Customer messaging and support platform with inbox, tickets, help center and Fin AI agent.
access_detail: Free development workspaces are available with no paid plan needed (US-only, 20-user max, cannot become production). Public apps use OAuth 2.0 via the Developer Hub. Private apps use access tokens on an existing workspace. Production Intercom workspaces are paid, but building and testing is free. I did not check whether the OAuth app directory listing needs review.
blocker_detail: None. Webhooks are supported per my background knowledge; the overview page I opened did not cover them. The official MCP is mostly read-only with 13 tools, so a REST toolkit still adds value.

one_liner: Cloud customer support helpdesk with ticketing, contacts, agents, and automation, by Freshworks.
access_detail: The pricing page lists no free plan. There is a 14-day trial with Enterprise-plan access. The API key comes from the user's profile settings and is sent over HTTP Basic. Docs say API access is role-based and rate-limited per plan (Blossom/Garden 3,000/hr). I did not find a per-plan API on/off gate; the pricing page does not say. Freshworks has an OAuth 2.0 flow for external apps, but I could not confirm it covers the Freshdesk v2 REST API, so I treat API key as primary.
blocker_detail: There is no free plan, only a 14-day trial, so ongoing testing needs a paid Freshdesk account or repeated trials. Auth is per-account API key; OAuth for the v2 REST API is unconfirmed. I did not verify webhooks.

one_liner: Shared inbox and customer communication platform for support teams across email, SMS and social channels.
access_detail: Front has no free tier. It offers a 14-day Professional trial with no credit card, and the OAuth app or API token is created inside a Front account. Creating apps requires company admin. The docs don't state a minimum plan for API access, so it's unverified whether the API stays available on Starter after the trial. Public App Store publishing requires notifying Front.
blocker_detail: There is no free tier. Testing needs a 14-day trial, then a paid plan (Starter is $25/seat/month) to keep a test workspace. OAuth is available to third-party apps with no documented approval step for development. Published App Store apps need Front's involvement.

one_liner: B2B support platform unifying Slack, email and chat support with issues, accounts, and AI agents.
access_detail: API tokens are generated in the dashboard (Settings > API tokens) by a Pylon customer workspace. Pricing page shows only a demo-booking flow, with no public free tier or trial. Whether a sandbox or free dev account exists was not found. OAuth2 exists only for the hosted MCP server (AuthKit), not documented as a general third-party app OAuth for the REST API.
blocker_detail: Pylon is sales-led (demo booking) with no visible free tier or self-serve signup. Getting a token requires a customer workspace. Webhooks were not verified.

one_liner: Help desk and live chat platform with ticketing, contacts, and multichannel support.
access_detail: No free plan. 30-day free trial with no credit card. API v3 keys are created by an admin in Configuration > System > API, and the pricing page lists API keys in every paid tier. Each account lives on its own domain (https://<domain>.ladesk.com/api/v3), so users must supply their domain plus key. OAuth 2.1 exists only for the built-in MCP server, not for the REST API.
blocker_detail: Testing needs a 30-day trial, and production use needs a paid plan. There is no permanent free tier. Auth is per-account key plus a per-tenant domain, and there is no third-party OAuth for the REST API. I did not verify webhooks. A QualityUnit GitHub MCP repo also exists, and the vendor's built-in MCP is at /api/mcp.

one_liner: API-first customer support platform for B2B teams, with a GraphQL API and threads/customers.
access_detail: Machine-user API keys are created in workspace settings. Pricing page shows a 7-day free trial with no credit card. It lists "API" under Extensibility but doesn't say which plans include it. I found no permanent free tier. I did not confirm whether API access is limited to paid tiers.
blocker_detail: Only a 7-day trial was found, with no free tier. The API docs describe only per-workspace API keys, not third-party OAuth, so each customer must generate and share a key. The official MCP uses OAuth, but for MCP clients, not a general third-party OAuth app program. The docs I opened did not mention webhooks; I did not check whether Plain offers them.

one_liner: Shared-inbox customer support platform with conversations, customers, docs, and reporting.
access_detail: Pricing page lists API access only on Standard, Plus and Pro. The Free plan has no API access listed. Standard and Plus have a 15-day no-card trial. An OAuth app can be created in a trial account. I did not verify whether a trial account can create OAuth apps, or whether the Free plan actually blocks the API.
blocker_detail: API access is listed only on paid plans (Standard $25/user/mo and up). The free plan shows none, so testing needs a 15-day trial or a paid seat.

one_liner: Ecommerce-focused helpdesk and AI support agent, popular with Shopify brands.
access_detail: Private apps use an API key (HTTP Basic with account email + API key) from a trial or paid helpdesk. Public multi-tenant apps must use OAuth2: register on the Developer Portal, create a draft app, get a Sandbox/Developer-plan account by emailing Gorgias tech partners, and submit the app for review. Trial length and API availability on trial not confirmed.
blocker_detail: Public OAuth2 apps require a draft app to obtain a sandbox (granted manually by Gorgias) and submission for review before listing. Private API-key use only needs a trial or paid helpdesk.

one_liner: Customer service platform with unified conversations, customer profiles, and AI agents for support teams.
access_detail: API tokens are created in the Gladly UI by a user an admin has granted the API User permission; the token is used as the Basic auth password with the agent email as username. Gladly is sold via sales contract with no found public signup or free tier. A sandbox exists at {organization}.gladly.qa but is tied to an existing customer org. Gating rests partly on absence of evidence of self-serve signup.
blocker_detail: Credentials require an existing paying Gladly customer org (sales contract); no free developer account or partner program was found. Tokens are per-user Basic auth, and no third-party OAuth is documented in the REST docs (the developer-platform marketing page mentions "OAuth authentication" only generically). Building requires a customer's org or sandbox.

one_liner: Team messaging platform with channels, DMs, files, canvases and workflow automation.
access_detail: Anyone can create an app and install it via OAuth 2.0, and public distribution is possible without Marketplace listing. Constraint: since May 29, 2025, new commercially distributed apps not approved for the Marketplace get stricter rate limits on conversations.history and conversations.replies. Marketplace approval is recommended for commercial distribution. I did not open a page confirming a free developer sandbox or the free-workspace API limits, so those are unverified.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker. Soft friction: non-Marketplace commercial apps face tight rate limits on conversations.history and conversations.replies, so Marketplace review is advisable for production scale. The official MCP server is limited to Marketplace-published and internal apps, but the toolkit would use the Web API directly, so that does not block it.

one_liner: Cloud communications platform APIs for SMS, voice, video, WhatsApp, email and verification.
access_detail: Anyone can sign up for a free trial and get the same Account SID/Auth Token immediately. The trial expires after 30 days and is limited to verified numbers (up to 5) and the sign-up country. Full use needs a paid upgrade (pay-as-you-go). Twilio also publishes free test credentials, which I did not open, so I can't confirm what they cover. Sub-account and ISV/Connect-style multi-tenancy exists but I did not verify it. SMS in the US also needs A2P 10DLC registration for production, which I did not verify on a page.
blocker_detail: No OAuth for third-party apps was found on the pages I opened. Users supply an Account SID plus an API key or Auth Token. The free trial works for building but is time-limited (30 days) and restricted to verified recipients. Production use needs an upgrade and paid usage.

one_liner: Team chat and collaboration platform from Zoho with channels, bots, and a REST API.
access_detail: Anyone can register an OAuth client at the Zoho API developer console for free. Cliq has a Free plan whose pricing page lists API support and limited bots, functions and custom integrations. The docs don't say the REST API is paid-only. I did not check per-plan API rate limits or whether some endpoints (e.g. admin/org-level) need a paid plan.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker found. Caveats: Zoho uses multiple data-center regions (.com, .eu, .in, etc.), so base URLs and OAuth endpoints vary per user. Free-plan limits apply.

one_liner: Team collaboration suite: messaging, docs, calendar, approvals, and base, with a broad open platform API.
access_detail: Anyone can create a custom app in the Developer Console and get App ID/Secret. Custom apps are single-tenant, so a test tenant is enough to build. Scopes need tenant admin approval. Multi-tenant distribution needs a Store App, which needs ISV certification and official review. I did not find pricing or plan gating for API access. Free Lark tenants appear to allow custom apps, but I did not verify this.
blocker_detail: Building and testing works today for free with a custom app in one tenant. Serving many customer tenants means publishing a Store App. That needs ISV certification and Lark's review. Each tenant admin must also approve scopes. Webhooks/events were not verified on a docs page, so that value comes from general knowledge.

one_liner: Team chat and messaging app from CAKE.com with channels, DMs, and a free plan.
access_detail: The API-keys addon is available on all plans, including Free, to Owner, Admin and Member roles. A user installs it via + Add apps and generates a key with no approval. The Pumble Apps SDK, which uses an app key and OAuth, is also self-serve, but I could not open its OAuth doc, so OAuth details are unverified from vendor pages.
blocker_detail: No blocker for the API-key path. The main uncertainty is whether OAuth2 for third-party multi-workspace apps is publicly documented and self-serve. The official MCP server uses a user or bot token plus an x-app-token, not a standard OAuth flow.

one_liner: Chat platform with servers, channels, DMs and voice; REST API and bot gateway for apps.
access_detail: Anyone can create an application and bot token in the Developer Portal at no cost. The docs I opened don't mention fees. Some OAuth2 scopes (voice, rpc, dm_channels.read) need Discord approval. From memory, not verified on a page I opened: bots in 100+ servers need verification, and privileged intents need approval. I did not open a pricing page.
blocker_detail: No blocker for building and testing. Scale friction to expect: restricted scopes need Discord approval, and (from memory, unverified) bots in 100+ servers need verification. A user-level OAuth2 toolkit can't send messages as the user, so most actions need a bot token, and guild admins have to install that bot.

one_liner: Messaging platform with a free Bot API for automating chats, channels, and groups.
access_detail: Anyone can create a bot by messaging @BotFather and get a token instantly, free and with no approval. Bots act only as bots, not as user accounts. Acting as a user would need MTProto (TDLib) with api_id/hash and a user login, which I did not open.
blocker_detail: No access blocker. Design caveat: there is no OAuth for acting on behalf of users. Each tenant must supply its own bot token, and bots can only message users who have started them. Community MCP servers found are mostly MTProto/Telethon user-account based. I found no official MCP.

one_liner: Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform Cloud API for sending/receiving messages, templates, and media at scale.
access_detail: Self-serve Meta developer signup gives a temporary token and test number for free. For multi-tenant use via Embedded Signup, the app needs Meta App Review (advanced access) and, for scale, Business Verification. Onboarding is capped at 10 customers per 7 days until verified. Customers must add a payment method, and template messages are charged per message.
blocker_detail: Onboarding customers via Embedded Signup requires Meta App Review (advanced access) and Business Verification for scale. Each customer also needs a payment method for template messages. Development and testing work free with a test number. The official MCP is only known from TechCrunch coverage; I did not open Meta's own announcement or repo. It appears aimed at account setup rather than general messaging. I did not verify the OAuth details, and Embedded Signup issues business tokens rather than a classic OAuth flow.

one_liner: Cloud phone/call-center system with calls, SMS, contacts, and AI voice agents.
access_detail: OAuth2 client_id/client_secret are issued only after submitting a Technology Partner application form. Without that, a customer can generate api_id/api_token (Basic auth) in Company Settings, but this needs a paid Aircall account (Essentials $30/license/month, min 3 users). No free sandbox or dev account was found. The free trial covers only AI Voice Agent minutes. I did not find explicit docs on whether API access is gated by plan tier. The Enterprise tier lists "API developer support".
blocker_detail: Multi-tenant OAuth2 requires acceptance into the Aircall Technology Partner program. Testing otherwise needs a paid Aircall account (min 3 users) with a customer-generated API key. No free sandbox was found.

one_liner: Communications APIs for SMS, voice, messaging channels, verification, video, and number management.
access_detail: Self-serve signup gives free test credit (about €2) in demo mode. Demo mode limits sends to about 5 verified numbers, adds an SMS watermark, and blocks number purchases. Adding funds removes these limits. Building and testing works at $0 with no approval, but production use needs prepaid funds. Trial limits come from search snippets of the support article, which I did not open directly.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker. Demo-mode limits (5 verified recipients, watermarked SMS, no number purchase) apply until funds are added. There is no OAuth for third-party apps, so each tenant supplies their own API key/secret or an application ID with a private key for JWTs. The vendor MCP servers are a documentation server and a tooling server in the Vonage-Community org. Whether the tooling server counts as official is unverified.

one_liner: Google's advertising platform; API manages campaigns, ad groups, assets, conversions, and reporting.
access_detail: OAuth2 plus a developer token are required. Access levels (Test/Explorer/Basic/Standard) are granted to the Cloud project. Test access only works against test accounts. Basic access needs brand verification, and its application is now automated and reviewed within minutes. Standard also needs approval. The API is free; the pages I opened list no fees. OAuth consent screen verification for the sensitive adwords scope was not checked in the docs.
blocker_detail: A developer token with Basic or Standard access is needed for production. It requires Cloud project brand verification, and Basic is reviewed automatically within minutes. Test accounts allow building without approval. Google may also require OAuth app verification for the sensitive scope. I did not confirm this on the pages I opened.

one_liner: Meta Marketing API to create, manage and report on Facebook/Instagram ad campaigns.
access_detail: Free self-serve developer account and app. Standard access to ads_read/ads_management works for your own ad account only. Managing other users' ad accounts (multi-tenant) needs Advanced access through App Review, plus business verification. I did not verify the exact App Review timelines.
blocker_detail: Advanced access for ads_read/ads_management needs Meta App Review and business verification before the app can act for other users' ad accounts. Development against your own ad account works without it. Webhook support for ads was not checked. A sandbox was not verified either; the free dev account is inferred from the docs.

one_liner: LinkedIn Marketing/Advertising API for managing ad accounts, campaigns, creatives, reporting, audiences and lead gen.
access_detail: Self-serve developer app, but Advertising API product needs LinkedIn application approval (Development tier). Dev tier allows unlimited reads and edits on up to 5 ad accounts. Standard tier (unlimited edits, needed for multi-tenant production) requires a support ticket and is at LinkedIn's discretion. No fee found for API access; approval timelines were not stated.
blocker_detail: Advertising API access requires LinkedIn app approval. Standard tier, needed to edit more than 5 ad accounts, requires a support ticket and is discretionary. Only 3-legged OAuth works for marketing use, with no client-credentials flow. Webhook support for Ads was not verified; only Community Management webhooks were mentioned. The sandbox rating rests on the Development tier plus one test ad account creatable via the API, not on a documented sandbox page.

one_liner: All-in-one CRM, marketing automation, funnels and messaging platform for agencies (HighLevel/LeadConnector).
access_detail: Marketplace developer account and Private apps allow OAuth app creation for testing; installing into a real account needs a HighLevel account. Pricing page shows a 14-day free trial, paid plans from $97/mo; API/Private Integration tokens tied to a paid account (trial or plan). Public marketplace apps need HighLevel review. I did not confirm whether a permanent free developer sandbox exists.
blocker_detail: Testing needs a HighLevel account: 14-day trial, then a paid plan ($97+/mo; Unlimited $297 includes basic API access, Agency Pro advanced API). Public listing needs app review. Webhooks were not verified on the docs pages I opened (based on general knowledge).

one_liner: Email marketing platform with audiences, campaigns, automations, reports and e-commerce via the Marketing API v3.
access_detail: A free plan (under 250 contacts) exists. API keys and OAuth app registration (Registered Apps page) are self-serve with no approval. The pricing page does not explicitly confirm API access on the free tier; it is inferred from general knowledge and the self-serve app registration.
blocker_detail: No blocking gate found. Minor caveats: free-tier API access is not explicitly stated on the pricing page, and OAuth tokens are tied to a data-center suffix (dc) that must be looked up via the metadata endpoint. The only official MCP covers Transactional, not Marketing.

one_liner: Email/SMS marketing automation and customer data platform for ecommerce brands.
access_detail: A free plan exists (up to 250 active profiles, 500 monthly sends) and private API keys can be created by Owner/Admin/Manager roles. Pricing page did not explicitly confirm API on free tier. OAuth for third-party apps is described as required for App Marketplace listing, so a public OAuth app may need Klaviyo partner/marketplace registration (not verified).
blocker_detail: No hard blocker found. Minor uncertainty: OAuth for third-party apps may require partner/marketplace registration; private API keys work immediately. Webhook availability not verified (webhook docs page returned 404).

one_liner: All-in-one marketing platform: funnels, email, courses, payments, blogs, affiliate programs.
access_detail: Free plan (no card, never expires) lets users generate up to 3 public API keys under profile settings. The docs and pricing page do not state which plans include API access, only that API requests per minute differ by plan. I found no evidence that the free plan blocks the API, but I did not confirm it either.
blocker_detail: No OAuth for third-party apps, so each user must paste a per-account API key. Per-plan rate limits apply, and API access by plan is unconfirmed.

one_liner: Visual discovery platform; API v5 for pins, boards, ads, audiences, catalogs and analytics.
access_detail: Self-serve app registration, but an app request must first be reviewed and approved for Trial access. Trial is sandbox-only, with content visible only to its creator and daily per-app rate limits. Production use needs an upgrade to Standard access, which requires a video demo of the OAuth flow and a review by Pinterest.
blocker_detail: Trial access requires app approval, and Trial content is sandbox-only. Real multi-user production use needs the Standard upgrade review, which includes a video demo of the OAuth flow. Search results also mention a Pinterest open-source MCP server for approved advertiser partners. I did not open that page, so I could not confirm it is official.

one_liner: Meta's Threads API for publishing posts, managing replies, reading media and insights.
access_detail: Self-serve Meta app via the Threads use case, free. Dev-mode testers (invited via App Dashboard) work without review. Serving public users needs Meta app review for threads_* permissions; that page was not opened, so this is from general Meta practice.
blocker_detail: Meta app review is needed to use threads_* permissions with users outside app roles and testers. Long-lived tokens last 60 days and must be refreshed. Media must be at a public URL.

one_liner: Twilio's cloud email delivery platform: transactional email API/SMTP plus marketing campaigns.
access_detail: Free trial gives 100 emails/day for 60 days, no credit card required. There is no permanent free tier after the trial; a paid plan (Essentials from $19.95/mo) is needed to continue. API keys are created in the console after signup with no human approval. Sender identity verification is required before sending.
blocker_detail: Testing works only during the 60-day trial (100 emails/day); ongoing use needs a paid plan. Per-user API keys only, with no OAuth for third-party apps. Twilio's official twilio-labs/mcp does not cover the SendGrid v3 API.

one_liner: Ecommerce platform with GraphQL Admin API for products, orders, customers, and app extensions.
access_detail: Developers can create apps in the Dev Dashboard and test on development stores. I did not confirm from the docs that dev stores are free; this is from prior knowledge. Installing a public multi-store app on merchant stores requires Shopify app approval. Custom apps for a single store or a Plus org need no approval. Protected customer data access also needs approval.
blocker_detail: A public app that installs on many merchants' stores needs Shopify approval. The official Dev MCP covers docs and schema only, not store operations. I found no store-operations MCP in the docs I opened. I did not search for community MCP servers.

one_liner: Open-source WordPress ecommerce plugin with a REST API for products, orders, customers, coupons.
access_detail: WooCommerce is a free, self-hosted plugin. A developer can run a local or hosted WordPress+WooCommerce store at $0 and generate a Consumer Key/Secret in WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API. No vendor approval was found. Pricing page was not opened; the free-plugin claim is from general knowledge. Each merchant store has its own base URL and keys, so a multi-tenant toolkit must collect store URL plus key/secret per user. The /wc-auth/v1/authorize endpoint (key auto-generation flow) was only inferred from the docs line about auto-generated keys, not opened.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker. Friction: the API is per-store and self-hosted, so each user supplies a store URL plus consumer key/secret (no central OAuth2 app). HTTP stores need OAuth 1.0a; HTTPS is recommended. The native MCP feature is in developer preview and uses WordPress Application Passwords.

one_liner: SaaS ecommerce platform with REST and GraphQL APIs for catalog, orders, customers, and storefronts.
access_detail: Developers can create apps in the Developer Portal (client ID/secret, OAuth install flow) and get a free sandbox store through the Partner Portal. Store owners can also generate store-level API tokens (X-Auth-Token). The sandbox duration, the exact partner sign-up approval, and any plan restrictions are not stated in the pages I opened. Marketplace listing requires review, but that is not needed to build or test.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker found. Sandbox access goes through the Partner Portal, so partner sign-up is an unverified small friction point.

one_liner: Enterprise B2C ecommerce platform with SCAPI/OCAPI APIs for catalog, baskets, orders, customers and promotions.
access_detail: Not verified from official pages: developer.salesforce.com returned HTTP 403 to my fetches, so the auth, pricing and API reference pages could not be opened. Search snippets and background knowledge say credentials come from an Account Manager API client on a customer or partner B2C realm. Sandboxes are allocated to a paid customer or partner realm. I found no free self-serve signup. Shopper APIs use SLAS with a per-tenant short-code, tenant-id and slas-client-id.
blocker_detail: A working toolkit needs a B2C Commerce realm or sandbox from a Salesforce contract or partner program. This is inferred, not confirmed from official pages, because the docs returned 403. Salesforce also ships an official MCP server (the B2C Developer Toolkit) that overlaps with a Composio toolkit.

one_liner: Open-source and commercial ecommerce platform with REST/GraphQL APIs for catalog, orders, customers and admin.
access_detail: The API ships with every install. Each merchant hosts its own instance (Open Source is free to self-host; Adobe Commerce is licensed or cloud). Credentials come from the store admin, either an admin or customer token or an OAuth 1.0a integration key set. There is no central developer signup. Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service uses Adobe IMS tokens, which I did not open in detail. I did not verify pricing pages, and the free Open Source claim comes from general knowledge.
blocker_detail: There is no hosted multi-tenant developer sandbox. Testing needs a self-installed Open Source instance or a customer's own store, and each user supplies their own base URL and token. The main auth methods are per-store tokens or OAuth 1.0a, not OAuth2 for third-party apps. Webhooks are asserted from general knowledge (Adobe Commerce webhooks and events modules) and were not verified.

one_liner: Website and ecommerce platform with REST Commerce APIs for orders, products, inventory, profiles and webhooks.
access_detail: OAuth for multi-tenant apps requires registering as an OAuth client; Squarespace reviews it and replies with client_id/secret. Per-merchant API keys are self-generated but need a Commerce Advanced plan. Neither is free without a paid site. A sandbox or free dev account was not found.
blocker_detail: OAuth client registration must be reviewed by Squarespace. The API-key fallback needs a merchant on the Commerce Advanced plan. The official MCP server only covers domain search (2 read-only tools), not commerce. The Webhook Subscriptions API is OAuth-only. The exact review turnaround and the paid-plan need for testing OAuth were not confirmed.

one_liner: Ecwid by Lightspeed: hosted ecommerce storefront platform with REST API for products, orders, customers.
access_detail: Docs say only stores on paid plans can access the API. Ecwid gives a free paid-plan upgrade for test stores, but you must email them to request it. Private (custom) apps get access tokens for a single store. Public apps use OAuth2 and are listed on the App Market. I did not find a public-app review process on the pages I opened.
blocker_detail: API needs a paid-plan store. A free test-store upgrade is available by emailing Ecwid, which is a manual step. Public OAuth apps for multi-tenant use go through the App Market. I did not verify the review requirements. Private apps cannot be installed in other stores.

one_liner: Platform for creators to sell digital products, memberships and courses directly to customers.
access_detail: Any Gumroad account can create an application in Settings > Advanced to get client_id/secret and generate an access token. No paid plan is documented (Gumroad charges only a per-sale fee). I could not render the official gumroad.com/api page (empty on fetch), so this rests on search snippets, third-party docs and the MCP README. I saw no evidence of app review for OAuth apps.
blocker_detail: No blocker found. The official docs page did not render in my fetch, so details come from secondary sources. Gumroad has no separate sandbox, but a free seller account with test products works.

one_liner: Amazon's API for sellers and vendors to manage orders, listings, inventory, reports and fulfillment.
access_detail: Registering as an SP-API developer needs a primary account user and, for private seller apps, a professional seller account. Public apps must be listed in the Selling Partner Appstore, which involves Amazon review and developer profile approval. Roles are requested and approved by Amazon. Fees are not stated on the pages I opened. I did not open the sandbox page, so sandbox availability and free-tier details are unverified.
blocker_detail: Developer registration and role approval are required. Production multi-tenant use needs a public app listed in the Selling Partner Appstore, which Amazon reviews. It also needs a professional seller account to test.

one_liner: Creator/enterprise payments platform: checkout, subscriptions, customers, products, refunds, disputes, webhooks.
access_detail: Docs say every request needs an x-api-key header, with scoped keys and a separate sandbox key and base URL. Docs don't say where keys are created or whether a plan or approval is needed. Free access is inferred, not confirmed. A newer docs portal (dev-docs.fanbasis.com, v3) sits behind a password login.
blocker_detail: The API-key signup path and any plan or approval requirement are not documented in the pages I could open. The v3 docs portal is password-gated. The public docs are a repo (otniel-bit/fbnewapi) that appears to be a mirror or fork, and the site it deploys is titled "Commas API Reference".

one_liner: Pay-as-you-go SEO data APIs: SERP, keywords, backlinks, on-page, labs, and more.
access_detail: Any registered user gets API login/password and free unlimited Sandbox access (sandbox.dataforseo.com, no charge). Live production calls need funded balance (pricing page: $50 minimum payment). The docs mention a free trial, but its terms were not opened.
blocker_detail: Only Basic auth with per-account API credentials for the API itself. The sandbox is free for building and testing. Production data needs prepaid credits ($50 minimum). Webhook/pingback support was not verified.

one_liner: SEO platform with rank tracking, keyword, backlink, site audit and AI-search visibility data via API.
access_detail: API key comes from account Settings > API. The API is bundled with paid subscriptions (from about $129/mo), or the API Add-On (from $149/mo), or pay-as-you-go (about $50 minimum). It can be tested in a no-card free trial. I did not verify the trial's API credit limits or duration. OAuth 2.1 appears only on the MCP server.
blocker_detail: No permanent free tier. API needs a paid plan, an add-on, or pay-as-you-go credits. Testing is limited to a free trial. Webhooks were not checked. An official hosted MCP already exists, which reduces the value of a new toolkit.

one_liner: SEO platform for backlinks, keywords, rank tracking and site audits, exposed via REST API v3 and MCP.
access_detail: API v3 requires a paid Ahrefs subscription (Lite or higher per the Help Center; older/third-party sources say Enterprise only). Workspace owners and admins create API keys used as bearer tokens. Free test queries exist for some endpoints without an Enterprise plan, but they don't give general access. A generic OAuth2 flow for third-party apps is not confirmed; the docs mention OAuth 2.0 only under the "Ahrefs Connect" partner integration program. Plan/unit numbers conflict between sources (Help Center: Lite 200k units/month; other sources: 100k). The MCP server is a hosted remote server for Lite and higher.
blocker_detail: A paid Ahrefs plan (Lite or higher, possibly Enterprise for some features) is needed for real API use. There is no free tier; only limited free test queries. Multi-tenant use means each end user brings their own API key, since third-party OAuth is unconfirmed. I could not open the docs.ahrefs.com auth page or the pricing page directly (404s), so the details come from the docs landing page, the Help Center and search results.

one_liner: AI-powered web scraping platform with unblocker, scraper agents, proxies and REST APIs.
access_detail: Free plan at $0/month with 1,000 tokens monthly, no credit card. API token copied from dashboard account settings (API Token page). Pro is $199/month for 200k tokens; extra usage $1 per 1,000 tokens.
blocker_detail: No blocker found. Free tier is token-limited (1,000/month). Webhook support was not verified; the docs list a Webhook integration, but it is likely outbound delivery of scrape results and I did not open it. The hosted MCP is described by search results as official, but the only repo I opened (a Claude plugin) is marked as unofficial marketplace testing. It reportedly uses OAuth for the MCP, but the API itself uses a per-account token.

one_liner: Cloud platform for web scraping and automation via prebuilt and custom Actors, with datasets and storage.
access_detail: Free plan with no credit card and $5 monthly prepaid usage. The pricing page doesn't explicitly say the free plan includes API access, but the API token is available in every account's Console (Integrations page). Paid Actors or higher usage need paid plans or credits.
blocker_detail: No blocker for building. Apify's OAuth appeared in docs for the hosted MCP server, and I could not confirm a general OAuth2 flow for third-party apps (the OAuth doc URL I tried returned 404). Per-user API tokens are the confirmed method for a multi-tenant toolkit.

one_liner: Web data API for AI agents: search, scrape, crawl, map, and extract clean markdown/JSON.
access_detail: Free plan with 1,000 credits/month, no credit card, API included (2 concurrent requests, low rate limits). Keyless access also documented for initial testing. Keys are created in the dashboard.
blocker_detail: None. Free tier is enough to build and test. Webhook support was not verified on the pages opened (crawl/batch webhooks likely exist, but I did not confirm). The docs describe an OAuth sign-in for the MCP server only. I found no documented OAuth for third-party apps on the REST API, so primary auth is api_key.

one_liner: Web data platform: proxies, Web Unlocker, SERP API, scrapers, and scraping browser.
access_detail: Account signup gives an API key from account settings. The official MCP offers 5,000 free requests per month with no credit card. The main API products (proxies, Web Unlocker, SERP) are pay-as-you-go. I could not confirm from the pricing page whether a free trial credit or minimum deposit applies to the REST APIs, so the free path for direct API testing is unverified.
blocker_detail: No approval or partnership is needed. Heavy usage of the REST APIs costs money, and I did not verify a free credit for them. No OAuth is offered, so it is per-user API key. Webhook support was not confirmed.

one_liner: Open-source CLI that checks a username across 400+ social networks.
access_detail: Sherlock is a local MIT-licensed CLI (pipx/docker/dnf). There is no vendor-hosted API or service and no credentials. Only wrappers exist, such as third-party Apify actors, which are not the vendor's. Pricing and API-reference pages do not exist. Could not confirm this from a full docs sweep; only the GitHub README and the homepage were opened.
blocker_detail: It is a local CLI with no hosted API. A Composio toolkit would need to run the tool itself, or wrap third-party Apify actors, which would bring their own auth and paid usage.

one_liner: B2B waterfall data enrichment: contact/company enrichment, prospecting, email verification, job-change detection across 30+ sources.
access_detail: Pricing page has no public tiers or self-serve signup; custom quotes after a free benchmark on your data. Docs don't say how to get a first key. Not verified whether a self-serve signup exists.
blocker_detail: No public pricing or self-serve signup found. Credits come via a sales-led commitment or benchmark. The docs are public and complete, so the toolkit can be written, but testing needs a key from sales. No sandbox is documented.

one_liner: GTM data enrichment and workflow platform aggregating 150+ data providers, AI research agents, and tables.
access_detail: Self-serve API keys (Settings > Account > API keys, beta, or `clay api-keys create`). Clay docs say the developer platform is available on all plans including free and trial. The Free plan (no card) includes 100 data credits/mo and 500 actions/mo, so a developer can get working credentials at $0 with low limits. Some endpoints are gated (Tables marked Enterprise, Workflows alpha).
blocker_detail: No approval or paid plan is needed to get a key. Per-account API keys only (no OAuth for third-party apps found). The API is beta, and Free plan credits are small (100 data credits/mo). Tables endpoint needs Enterprise. Rate limits were not verified.

one_liner: Code hosting and developer platform: repos, issues, PRs, Actions, and orgs, exposed via REST and GraphQL APIs.
access_detail: Free GitHub account can create OAuth Apps, GitHub Apps and personal access tokens with no approval. Orgs may restrict third-party app access, which the org owners can approve. This was not verified on the pages I opened. Pricing page not opened. Free-tier API availability is well known but not quoted.
blocker_detail: No blocker for building. OAuth/GitHub App can be registered self-serve with a free account. Org-level app approval by org owners may be needed per customer.

one_liner: Frontend cloud platform for deploying web apps, with projects, domains, deployments, and edge infrastructure.
access_detail: Free Hobby plan ($0/mo) with no documented API restriction by plan; users generate access tokens in the dashboard, and third-party apps can register Sign in with Vercel (OAuth 2.0) apps self-serve. I did not open the OAuth getting-started page, so the exact scope coverage of REST API endpoints and any approval step are unverified. Some features, such as team-level ones, need Pro.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker found. I did not verify the OAuth scope granularity for third-party apps, and webhooks are inferred from the get_webhook and drains tools and endpoints rather than a page I opened.

one_liner: Web hosting and deployment platform with serverless functions, forms, DNS, and CI/CD for sites.
access_detail: Free plan ($0 forever) includes deploying via API. Personal access tokens are self-generated in user settings. OAuth2 apps are registered in user settings with no approval step documented. Some granular env var scopes are Pro-only.
blocker_detail: No blocker found. Webhooks are inferred from the API reference listing hooks and build hooks. I did not open a dedicated webhook docs page.

one_liner: CDN, DNS, security, and edge developer platform (Workers, R2) managed via a broad REST API.
access_detail: Anyone can sign up for a free Cloudflare account and create user or account API tokens in the dashboard. Account-owned tokens are available for all accounts. I found no plan gate on token creation. I did not open a page that states free-plan API access outright, so that part is inferred from the docs and search results. Creating account-owned tokens needs Super Administrator on the account. I found no documented OAuth2 flow for third-party apps in the pages I opened, so a multi-tenant toolkit would have users paste tokens. Legacy Global API Key (X-Auth-Key) also exists.
blocker_detail: No blocker for building and testing today. The one caveat is that OAuth2 for third-party apps was not found in the opened docs, so end users must supply their own API tokens.

one_liner: Open-source Postgres backend platform with auth, storage, realtime and edge functions.
access_detail: Free plan at $0 (2 active projects, paused after 1 week of inactivity). Management API accepts a PAT or OAuth2 token. Third-party OAuth apps are created in org settings. The docs page I opened mentions no vendor approval step. Per-project data APIs (PostgREST) use project API keys and are not covered by this toolkit's OAuth path.
blocker_detail: No blocker found. The free tier and OAuth apps are self-serve. Webhooks support was not verified; the Management API page lists "analytics and webhooks" but I did not open a dedicated webhooks page. I did not verify whether OAuth apps need review before publishing.

one_liner: Graph database (Aura cloud and self-managed) queried with Cypher; Aura API manages cloud instances.
access_detail: Aura API credentials (client ID/secret, OAuth2 client-credentials) can be created on all tiers, including Free, with no approval. Free/trial tier is rate-limited to 25 req/min. The Aura API only manages instances (create, resize, snapshot). Data access uses per-instance database credentials (username/password) over Bolt or the HTTP Query API. I could not confirm the Query API auth method from the page I opened. Aura Free and self-hosted Community are free for testing.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker. Caveats: the Aura API is a management API, not a data API, so a useful toolkit must also handle per-instance DB credentials and Cypher over the Query API. The Aura Free API rate limit is low at 25 req/min. The official MCP server is local (stdio) and uses username/password env vars.

one_liner: Cloud data platform for warehousing, analytics, and AI workloads, queried via SQL and REST APIs.
access_detail: Every Snowflake account is per-customer. Developers can get a 30-day trial with no credit card, or until the free credit balance runs out. After that the account is suspended and needs a paid upgrade. No permanent free tier was found. AI features on trial accounts need a credit card added. Snowflake OAuth needs a security integration created in the customer's account.
blocker_detail: Testing only works on a 30-day trial with limited credits, and there is no free tier after that. Each customer account also needs its own OAuth security integration (per-account host). Webhook support was not checked.

one_liner: Managed cloud MongoDB database service with an Administration API for clusters, projects, users and more.
access_detail: Anyone with an Atlas account (free M0 tier available) who is Organization Owner can create a service account (client ID/secret) or API keys. The docs I opened mention no plan restriction on the Admin API. I did not open a pricing page, so the free-tier claim is from general knowledge.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker. Two caveats: (1) Atlas offers no OAuth2 authorization-code flow for third-party apps, only per-organization service account (client-credentials OAuth2) or legacy digest API keys, so each user must generate credentials themselves. (2) Webhook support was not verified. Atlas does have alert webhooks, but I did not open docs on them.

one_liner: Cloud observability platform for metrics, logs, traces, monitors, dashboards and incidents.
access_detail: Auth uses per-org API key (DD-API-KEY) plus Application key (DD-APPLICATION-KEY) for read endpoints. The pricing page lists a Free Infrastructure tier (up to 5 hosts, 1-day retention) and free trials. The pricing page doesn't say whether API access is included in the free tier, and I didn't verify that free accounts can create keys. The API is also site/region-specific (datadoghq.com, .eu, etc.). OAuth for third-party apps is not mentioned on the authentication page I opened. The hosted MCP server does use OAuth, but I didn't confirm that from a page I opened.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker found. Users must create API and Application keys themselves and pick the correct Datadog site. The free tier is limited, and whether it includes API key creation was not verified. I did not confirm webhook support from the pages I opened.

one_liner: Application error monitoring, tracing and performance platform for developers.
access_detail: Free Developer plan exists and tokens/OAuth apps can be created self-serve. The pricing page fetch summary said the Developer plan lacks API access (Team+ has 'API & third-party integrations'). I could not confirm this against the plan-comparison table. It conflicts with my understanding that free orgs can create tokens. I could not open the integration-platform docs (rate limit), so I did not check for plan restrictions on OAuth public integrations. Treat free API access as likely but unverified.
blocker_detail: No firm blocker found. The pricing page suggested the free plan may lack API access, which would make this build_with_friction (paid plan). Unresolved.

one_liner: Workspace for docs, wikis, databases and project management, with a REST API.
access_detail: Public connections (OAuth 2.0) and internal connections (static token) are documented with no plan requirement stated. A free Notion workspace is widely known to allow integrations, but I did not verify this on a pricing page. Public OAuth apps need no vendor review as far as the docs show; this was not explicitly checked.
blocker_detail: No blocker found. Webhook support comes from my prior knowledge; I did not open a webhooks page. The free-tier API access claim was not verified on a pricing page.

one_liner: Cloud database/spreadsheet hybrid for building collaborative apps, workflows and tables.
access_detail: OAuth integrations are registered self-serve via Airtable's builder hub, and the OAuth reference describes no formal review step. Only ToS, support email and privacy policy URLs are needed outside development. The free-plan API and personal access token details come from prior knowledge, not from a page I opened. My session limit hit before I could open the pricing and API-introduction pages.
blocker_detail: No blocker found. Enterprise accounts can restrict third-party OAuth authorization for their users, but that is a per-customer limit, not a developer blocker.

one_liner: Issue tracking and project management tool for software teams, with a GraphQL API.
access_detail: Free plan (unlimited members, 2 teams, 250 issues) includes API and webhook access. Anyone can create a workspace and generate personal API keys or register OAuth2 apps with no approval step found.
blocker_detail: No blocker found. Free workspace has API and webhook access. OAuth2 (authorization code, PKCE, client_credentials) is available to third-party apps.

one_liner: Atlassian's issue and project tracking tool for software and business teams.
access_detail: Jira Cloud Free plan (up to 10 users, no time limit) gives a free site for testing. OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps are created in the developer console at no cost and are private by default. Sharing/distribution needs extra setup. The free-plan facts come from search snippets because the pricing page was truncated when fetched.
blocker_detail: No main blocker. Minor points: the OAuth app is private until sharing is enabled, and Atlassian says apps should ship a single distributable 3LO app. The webhooks value comes from my background knowledge, not from a page I opened.

one_liner: Work management platform for tasks, projects, and team collaboration with a REST API.
access_detail: Free Personal plan exists ($0, 2 users). The developer console lets anyone create an OAuth app and get a client ID and secret. Docs mention no plan requirement or review step. The pricing page does not state that the free plan includes API access, so this is unconfirmed. Users must have the app distributed to their workspace via "Manage distribution". Service accounts are probably an Enterprise feature; I did not verify this.
blocker_detail: No blocker found. Open questions are whether the free plan includes full API access and whether premium-only endpoints exist. Neither was confirmed in the docs I opened.

one_liner: Work management platform with boards, items, automations and dashboards, exposed via a GraphQL API.
access_detail: A free developer/sandbox account gives an API token and playground at $0 with no approval. OAuth2 apps can be created in the Developer Center. Marketplace listing requires review, but that isn't needed for OAuth use. Whether other accounts' API access depends on plan tier was not confirmed.
blocker_detail: No blocker found. A free developer account provides a token and OAuth app creation. Webhooks were not opened in the docs, so that value comes from general knowledge (GraphQL create_webhook).

one_liner: Work management platform for tasks, docs, goals, time tracking and team collaboration.
access_detail: Personal tokens (pk_) are generated in Settings > Apps, and OAuth apps can be created by Workspace owners/admins. The rate-limits page lists the FreeForever plan at 100 req/min and mentions no plan restriction on API access. I did not open the pricing page, so I did not check whether particular endpoints (e.g. some enterprise/AI features) need a paid plan.
blocker_detail: No blocker found. Rate limits are per token: 100 req/min on Free, Unlimited and Business plans, and higher on Business Plus and Enterprise. Webhooks were not verified on a page I opened. That is from prior knowledge.

one_liner: Collaborative doc and table workspace (now Superhuman Docs) with docs, pages, tables, rows and automations.
access_detail: The API is free for all users in free and paid workspaces. Each user generates a personal API token and sends it as a Bearer header. createDoc needs a Doc Maker or Admin role. Plan limits beyond that were not verified. OAuth2 (PKCE, single scope mcp:all) exists only for the MCP server, not the REST API.
blocker_detail: No paid plan, trial or approval step is needed. Each user pastes a personal API token; the REST API has no third-party OAuth. The MCP server supports OAuth2 PKCE or a PAT with the MCP restriction. The older coda.io/apis/mcp endpoint still works but is slated for deprecation. Coda has no webhook subscriptions; it only has webhook-invoked automations.

one_liner: Work management platform with sheets, rows, and workflows for project and team collaboration.
access_detail: API access needs a Business, Enterprise, or Advanced Work Management plan. Trial accounts reportedly cannot generate API tokens (from search snippets, not an opened page). Developer registration for OAuth apps and the sandbox requires an existing licensed Business-or-higher user. The Free plan has no API access. I did not open the pricing page.
blocker_detail: The API, MCP server, and developer registration all need a paid Business or higher plan. The free trial cannot generate API tokens. Registered developer sandbox accounts exist, but only for users already on a paid plan. Webhooks are inferred from the API reference, and I did not open that page.

one_liner: Time tracking, invoicing, expenses and project budgeting SaaS with REST API v2.
access_detail: Anyone with a Harvest ID can create a Personal Access Token or register an OAuth2 app in the Developers section. The free plan is $0 forever (1 seat, 2 projects). The pricing page doesn't say whether the free plan includes API access, and the docs I opened show no plan restriction or app review. A 30-day trial may also apply. Rate limits were not found.
blocker_detail: No blocker found. Unverified: the free plan's API access, since the pricing page is silent on it. Webhooks were not checked; I couldn't open the official MCP help page (HTTP 403), so its "official" status rests on a search snippet from Harvest's own help center.

one_liner: Payments platform with APIs for charges, subscriptions, invoicing, payouts, Connect, Issuing, Tax and Treasury.
access_detail: Signing up for a Stripe account creates API keys at no cost. Free sandboxes with sk_test_/rk_test_ keys and test data let you build and test with no approval. Live mode needs account activation. OAuth for third-party use goes through a Stripe App with distribution_type public. It can be tested via an External test link before submitting for App Marketplace review. Whether a review is needed to install on arbitrary accounts before publication was not confirmed. Pricing page not opened; there is no per-API fee, and payments are charged per transaction.
blocker_detail: No blocker for building and testing. Multi-tenant OAuth via Stripe Apps needs App Marketplace review to publish, which is a production-distribution step. Connect platform OAuth was not checked. The MCP server stops accepting non-agent secret keys and restricted keys on 31 Oct 2026, though this doesn't affect direct REST use.

one_liner: Financial data API connecting bank accounts for transactions, balances, identity, auth, and payments.
access_detail: Dashboard signup gives client_id and secret with a free Sandbox immediately. Production needs a separate access request via the Dashboard and Plaid approval. Limited Production allows up to 200 API calls per product on live data. Pay-as-you-go is the paid tier. Per-user access requires an end-user bank connection through Plaid Link (a user-facing UI flow) that yields an access_token.
blocker_detail: Production access needs a Plaid access request and approval. Sandbox is free for building and testing. Official MCP servers cover developer diagnostics and tooling (hosted Dashboard MCP for Production diagnostics; local Sandbox MCP in the AI coding toolkit), not end-user financial data. Not verified: the exact production approval criteria, or whether Plaid offers OAuth2 to third-party platforms. The Plaid Link flow must be hosted by the toolkit.

one_liner: Crypto exchange with REST/WebSocket APIs for spot, futures, wallet and account trading.
access_detail: Any verified Binance account holder can create API keys (HMAC/RSA/Ed25519) on the API Management page at no cost. A free Spot testnet issues keys via GitHub login. I did not find pricing pages, and I did not verify KYC requirements for live keys or any third-party OAuth program. Keys are per-account, so a multi-tenant toolkit would have users paste their own key and secret.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker. Users must supply their own API key and secret, and trading or withdrawal permissions are set per key. The financial risk from live trading is high, and the testnet covers Spot only, as far as I verified. Webhooks: none seen, since the docs offer WebSocket streams, not webhooks.

one_liner: NMI-powered payment gateway API for card payments, vaulting, recurring billing and transaction reporting.
access_detail: I found no Paygent Connect-specific developer docs. The Paygent results were for the unrelated Japanese Paygent Co. Docs are from NMI, the underlying platform. A free NMI sandbox account can be created without a merchant account. Live use needs a merchant account and gateway keys, likely via Paygent or a reseller, and that path was not verified.
blocker_detail: A toolkit can be built and tested against the free NMI sandbox. No vendor-approval step was found. Each merchant supplies its own key, so there is no shared OAuth. Whether Paygent Connect has its own portal or branded docs is unverified, so the target platform may be NMI itself. The webhook flag comes from the docs describing "event-driven integrations", not from a dedicated webhooks page.

one_liner: FINTRAC-registered FX forensic audit layer comparing bank/card FX rates to mid-market across 300+ currencies.
access_detail: Vendor MCP docs: dashboard-issued ipx_test_/ipx_live_ keys sent as an HTTP Bearer token; free tier of 10 audits/day and 60 rate checks/min per key. The GitHub README instead lists check_fx_rate and compare_fx_sources as no-auth and 3 free audits/month per IP. full_forensic_fx_report is paid ($199 tier). ipayx.ai/docs returns a 404 page.
blocker_detail: The public API is essentially an MCP endpoint with thin, inconsistent docs. The docs root is a 404, and the endpoints, free limits and auth requirements differ between the vendor MCP page (Supabase endpoint, per-key limits) and the GitHub README (Cloudflare worker endpoint, per-IP limits). The tool surface is narrow, and the full report is paid.

one_liner: Intuit's cloud accounting software; QuickBooks Online API for invoices, customers, payments, and reports.
access_detail: Free Intuit developer account and free sandbox companies with development keys (from prior knowledge; the Intuit docs pages returned truncated content, so this was not verified on-page). Production keys require completing Intuit's app assessment questionnaire and, for public listing, app review. Intuit's app partner program metering or tiers may also apply and were not verified.
blocker_detail: Sandbox development is free, but connecting real customer companies with production keys needs Intuit's app assessment and review. The Intuit docs pages (OAuth, sandbox, API reference) rendered as truncated JavaScript, so the free-sandbox and review details come from prior knowledge rather than opened pages. Webhooks are also from prior knowledge.

one_liner: Cloud accounting platform for small businesses: invoices, bank feeds, payroll, and reporting.
access_detail: Developers can sign up free, register an app, and use a Demo Company at no cost. Starter tier is free but capped at 5 connections and 1,000 calls/day for uncertified apps. Going past 5 connections needs payment details and the Core tier (35 AUD/month). The pricing page says tiers above Starter need app certification, and Advanced/Enterprise also need security assessments. The exact certification requirement for Starter could not be confirmed. The developer docs render as JS, so the OAuth page content was not readable.
blocker_detail: A production multi-tenant toolkit will exceed 5 connections on the free Starter tier. It then needs the paid Core tier or higher, plus app certification. A new policy also bans using Xero API data to train AI/ML, which needs a legal check for agent use.

one_liner: Corporate cards, expense, spend management, travel and bill pay platform for finance teams.
access_detail: Per-account user tokens are generated by account or card admins in the Brex dashboard, so you need a Brex customer account. OAuth2 for authenticating other Brex accounts is partner-only: apply to the partner program, a partner manager qualifies you, and you sign a Unilateral API Access Agreement. Staging accounts are provisioned by Brex on request. I could not open the partner_authentication page directly (404). Partner details come from search snippets of developer.brex.com.
blocker_detail: Multi-tenant OAuth2 requires acceptance into Brex's partner program and a signed API access agreement. Without it, only single-account user tokens from an existing Brex customer account are available. Staging is provisioned by request. If a per-user bearer-token toolkit is acceptable, this becomes build_with_friction.

one_liner: Corporate card, spend management, bill pay and expense automation platform for businesses.
access_detail: Ramp supports OAuth2 client credentials, authorization code and refresh token grants. Apps are created in the Ramp developer console (Profile > Developer > Create app). A sandbox exists at demo.ramp.com and demo-api.ramp.com. The docs do not state the sandbox signup process, cost or approval requirements, so free self-serve is inferred rather than confirmed. Public or listed third-party integrations go through a separate partner and technology-partnership program. The Ramp account itself is not confirmed as free. Some MCP connection controls are noted as available on Ramp Plus.
blocker_detail: No hard blocker found. Open questions are how sandbox signup works, whether it needs a Ramp account, and whether a public multi-tenant authorization-code app needs partner approval. The docs don't say.

one_liner: Private and public capital markets data platform covering companies, investors, deals, and funds.
access_detail: Direct Data API needs a separate contract on top of a PitchBook platform subscription. Pricing is quote-only, and existing customers request keys via the platform's Plugins & Apps section. A sandbox key is available on request from the account team. The vendor docs pages returned 403 to me, so most facts come from secondary sources (ZoomInfo review, search snippets).
blocker_detail: API requires an enterprise contract plus a platform subscription. There is no free tier or trial, and the docs are visible only to contracted clients. The official OAuth MCP connector exists, but it is for PitchBook subscribers and is not a third-party OAuth app program.

one_liner: Google's AI research notebook; Enterprise API manages notebooks, sources, and audio overviews.
access_detail: Only the Gemini Notebook Enterprise API (v1alpha, Pre-GA) is documented. It needs a Google Cloud project, Gemini Notebook Enterprise licenses (standalone or via Gemini Enterprise) and the Cloud NotebookLM User IAM role. Pricing was not on the pages I opened. The consumer NotebookLM has no public API.
blocker_detail: The API needs paid Gemini Notebook Enterprise licenses and a Google Cloud project. The API is Pre-GA v1alpha. Community MCPs drive the consumer product through browser cookies, which is a ToS and scraping risk. I did not confirm a free trial or the price.

one_liner: AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes, and summarizes meetings.
access_detail: Public REST API (beta) is only for Enterprise workspaces; the Enterprise admin generates a token (Enterprise Settings → API), otherwise contact the account manager. The official MCP server (https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp) uses OAuth for MCP clients, but I could not verify its plan requirements or whether it is usable as a third-party OAuth app for a multi-tenant toolkit. The help.otter.ai pages returned 403, so the plan and auth details come from search snippets and a third-party repo.
blocker_detail: The public API is a beta limited to Enterprise workspaces, with no self-serve or free developer path and no OAuth app registration. The official MCP is OAuth-based, which might be a workable alternative path, but its plan gating and third-party usability are unverified.

one_liner: AI meeting notetaker that records, transcribes and summarizes calls, with a public API.
access_detail: API keys are generated by any user in User Settings > API Access; docs state no plan requirement (plan gating not specified, so it is unconfirmed). OAuth apps are registered self-serve in a portal but are 'subject to review'. Rate limits exist but details were not retrieved.
blocker_detail: Dev testing works with a personal API key. Multi-tenant OAuth apps are reviewed by Fathom, though the docs describe self-serve registration in about 2 minutes. Whether the free plan includes API access was not confirmed in the docs I opened.

one_liner: AI search engine over 220M+ peer-reviewed papers, with a REST search API and hosted MCP server.
access_detail: Self-serve API keys are created from a Consensus account. The API help page lists included credits only for Pro/Team/Enterprise (500) and Deep (2,000), plus $0.05 per extra call. It doesn't say whether the Free plan gets API credits, so this is uncertain. The API and MCP share one monthly call pool by tier. The x-api-key header detail came from a search snippet, because docs.consensus.app returned 403 to fetches.
blocker_detail: OAuth is only for the MCP server, where users sign in with a Consensus account. No third-party OAuth app registration was found for the REST API, which uses per-account API keys. API credits appear tied to paid plans. Whether the Free plan has any API credits is unconfirmed. The docs site blocked fetching.

one_liner: Document parsing/extraction API turning PDFs and files into structured JSON for LLMs.
access_detail: Sign up at studio.reducto.ai, create an API key in Studio. Standard pay-as-you-go tier includes $150 (15,000 credits) of free usage, no approval needed.
blocker_detail: None. Free credits cover development, and the vendor's own MCP repo (reductoai org) already exists. I did not open the MCP docs page (it timed out), so its details are unverified.

one_liner: Cognition's autonomous AI software engineer; API manages sessions, knowledge, playbooks, schedules.
access_detail: API v3 covers Organization API (Teams/standard orgs) and Enterprise API (Enterprise). Credentials are cog_ service-user keys or personal access tokens, with no OAuth for third-party apps found. The pricing page shows a Free tier, but I could not confirm it includes org API access. Teams is $80/mo base plus $40 per developer. Assumed paid-plan gating, with moderate uncertainty.
blocker_detail: The API appears to be tied to Teams or Enterprise organizations, so it needs a paid plan. There is no OAuth for third-party apps, so each user must supply a cog_ key. Webhooks were not mentioned in the docs I opened.

one_liner: AI image/video generation platform aggregating 30+ models, with REST API, SDKs and hosted MCP.
access_detail: Keys are created in the Higgsfield Console after signup. The API is priced per second or per image, so generation needs paid credits. I did not find a documented free tier or free credits, so free access is unconfirmed. The hosted MCP uses an OAuth login to a Higgsfield account and draws on that account's credits. It is not documented as available to third-party OAuth apps.
blocker_detail: Generation is billed per second or per image against credits. I found no documented free tier for testing. Auth is a per-account key ID and secret, with no documented OAuth2 for third-party apps. I could not open the pricing or plan pages, so the free-credit status is unverified.

one_liner: Open-source CLI/Node library rendering Mermaid diagram definitions to SVG, PNG or PDF via Puppeteer.
access_detail: MIT-licensed local tool installed via npm or Docker. No account, credentials, pricing, or hosted API. Runs locally and needs headless Chromium (Puppeteer).
blocker_detail: There is no hosted API or per-user auth. A toolkit would have to run the CLI locally or in a container with Node and headless Chromium, so it fits a local-execution or sandbox toolkit rather than a multi-tenant API toolkit. Cost is $0 and nothing gates it.

one_liner: REST API and MCP server for YouTube transcripts, search, channel and playlist data.
access_detail: Signup gives 100 free credits with no card. Paid plan is about $5/month, plus top-up credits. 1 credit = 1 successful request. Free credits are enough to build and test, but they are a finite allowance, not a recurring free tier.
blocker_detail: No blocker. The 100 free credits run out, so heavy testing needs the roughly $5/month plan. Only a static per-account API key exists, with no OAuth. Webhooks were not seen in the docs. I did not verify the /docs/api endpoint pages or the exact auth docs page, only the homepage summary, docs overview and MCP blog post.

one_liner: AI meeting recorder and notetaker with transcripts, highlights, clips and CRM/deal insights.
access_detail: Personal API access (PAT) needs Starter or higher; Workspace tokens need Business/Enterprise admin; Free plan has no API access. OAuth2 for third-party apps is documented, but the registration process and any approval requirement were not found on the pages I opened. Whether a free trial unlocks the API is unconfirmed.
blocker_detail: API tokens require a paid plan (Starter or higher); the Free plan excludes API access. OAuth2 app registration terms were not verified.
